content:
September 16, 2026

Spend a week with me in Japan, where I take you through my adventures in Tokyo, Kyoto, Nara, and Osaka!

Day 1

After a hellish 14-hour flight to Taipei followed by another three hours to Tokyo, I FINALLY landed in Japan.

My first challenge: figuring out how the hell to get to my hotel.

I was having trouble paying for the train and, considering my Japanese is basically nonexistent, I was struggling. Thankfully, some locals noticed and helped me figure it out despite the language barrier. A very wholesome introduction to Japan after such a long day of travel.

I made it to the hotel just in time to meet my Contiki group, and our first night out was in Shinjuku.

Of course, I immediately got lost. I was still getting used to the Tokyo subway system, and thought that all exits led to the same place like the L back in Chicago. To help get myself “unlost”, for lack of a better term, I started sharing locations with my roommate to help me find the rest of the group. I took some pictures around Shinjuku for the Instagram feed, and we finished the night at a bar playing drinking games. I headed home relatively early since I was still jet-lagged.

Day 2

SO. MUCH. RAIN.

I started the morning by getting breakfast with my roommate and some of her friends before heading out to explore Tokyo. Our first stops were Sensō-ji in Asakusa and Meiji Shrine.

After that, I decided to go to Uniqlo and try some things on, but didn’t buy anything since I was short on time and had to meet the group before our next activity. Oh well. There are plenty of other opportunities to shop on this trip.

After that, we headed to Harajuku, where I got lunch. I had a Japanese egg sando, which was SO creamy and rich, as well as a matcha (despite already drinking TWO cups of coffee that morning. I know. I was stupid and thought extra caffiene would fix my jet lag).

And then I basically just went crazy shopping for the rest of the day. Did I take advantage of the weak yen, or did the weak yen take advantage of me? (Spoiler: it’s the latter)

Day 3

Update: The caffeine fix from yesterday did not work.

I only got 5 hours of sleep last night because of jet lag and I kept automatically waking up early because my circadian rhythm was messed up. I had a ticket to TeamLabs borderless in the morning, so I got up at like 7, walked around Minato/Tokyo tower, got some pictures, and went to the Azabudai Hills mall that TeamLabs Borderless was located in.

I spent about two hours inside, wandering through the exhibits without a set route—which is basically the entire point of Borderless. The artworks flow into one another and transform as you move through the space.

And, not gonna lie, I also spent a decent amount of time admiring my outfit in all the mirrors.

My favorite exhibit was “On the Asymmetry of the Universe”. Rays of light and color seemed to float through the space and change dynamically depending on the presence and behavior of the people inside. It was genuinely mesmerizing.

After that, I grabbed lunch at Azabudai Hills Market and got a salmon & veggie bento box and organic wine, which was pretty good but also overpriced.

For the rest of the day, I went back to Harajuku to do MORE shopping since I’m a shopaholic - I wanted to visit the Brandy Melville in Tokyo that I’ve seen all over TikTok, and I loved their Japan-exclusive styles that I couldn’t find in the states since they had that distinctly Y2K East Asian fashion aesthetic.

Day 4

I woke up early and took the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto. I was still tired, so I slept on the train ride. I was worried about missing the view of Mount Fuji, but it was so cloudy that I wouldn’t get a good view anyways.

After arriving at Kyoto Station, I grabbed okonomiyaki topped with oysters, squid, and an egg for lunch. It was delicious, but somehow I was full within approximately five bites.

After lunch, I was in a rush to catch up with the rest of the group since we were going on a tour bus so I left my umbrella behind. It was raining HARD because it was typhoon season in Japan.

Our first stop was Kinkaku-ji, the famous Golden Pavilion. Despite the weather, it was absolutely gorgeous, and obviously I got plenty of pictures for Instagram. The problem was that I no longer possessed an umbrella, so I had to “borrow” some umbrella space from a friend.

After exploring the Gion district, we had a short break, during which I immediately bought myself a new umbrella from 7-Eleven.

Then came Fushimi Inari. It was a very long hike, and it was still raining. However the rain eased up a little. I tried so hard not to slip on the steps since they were still slippery from the rain.

For dinner, I got ramen at the food hall at Kyoto Station.

Day 5

This morning I visited Nara Deer Park. It was about an hour of a train ride, and I had the opportunity to sleep on the train. As soon as I got there, it was raining pretty intensely. After seeing some deer, we visited some Buddhist temples, which were very photogenic places. I got lots of pictures. For lunch, I got cold ramen, which I thought was pretty good, but the meat was a bit too fatty. In the afternoon, I had a ticket for TeamLabs Biovortex. I almost skipped and I’m so glad I didn’t.

I honestly preferred this one to Borderless because it was a lot more hands-on and immersive, I especially loved the “Athletics Forest” where your movement could actively shape and influence the artwork around you. I had ramen again for dinner (wagyu ramen) and went to a karaoke bar.

And that night?

I had a few drinks and sang my lungs out.

10/10 cultural experience.

Day 6

This morning, I went to a kimono rental place, where I got dressed in a blue kimono, pink bag, pink hair accessory, and pink slides.

We then explored a historic neighborhood in Kyoto, and I had a matcha shaved ice. I got a lot of pictures of the views of the mountains and temples.

For lunch, I had black garlic tonkatsu ramen, and in the afternoon, I didn’t really do much. I just did laundry and packed for the next city I was about to visit, which was Osaka.

That night, I went out with friends to ZaZa Pub and some neighboring bars before dinner.

And dinner was…quite filled with complications.

We initially thought we’d ordered way too much food, so we tried to cancel everything. Then we realized we’d actually ordered the right amount. So now we had to reorder everything we had JUST canceled. Eventually, we literally wrote our names next to each dish we wanted and handed the list to the waiter. Finally the food arrived.

We didn’t finish eating until around 11 pm, which was later than I would’ve liked considering I had to wake up early AGAIN the next morning.

Day 7

Still sleep-deprived, I woke up early to catch the train to Osaka.

I was annoyed that all the seats were taken because I wanted to sleep some more, so I decided to attempt to sleep standing up. As soon as we arrived at Osaka, I mostly spent the day solo, walking around the mall and doing some shopping, buying various jewelry and shoes.

For lunch, I had a sashimi bowl with udon noodles, which ended up being one of my favorite meals of the trip.

Afterward, I kept wandering until hotel check-in opened at 3 PM. The SECOND I could check in, I did.

Then I took a fat two-hour nap.

Absolutely glorious.

I started packing because this trip was almost coming to an end (ALREADY???) and got dinner at this restaurant nearby (I wanted to branch out and explore new restaurants, since Osaka is known for its food scene). And then, for my final night in Japan, I went clubbing.

Day 8

And my trip’s a wrap. I had to get up early, got breakfast, took the train to Kansai Airport, took the plane to Taipei, got some beef noodles for dinner at Taoyuan Airport, and then took ANOTHER 14 hour flight, and landed back in Chicago.
title: Japan: Typhoons, TeamLab & Taking Advantage of the Weak Yen

content:
March 25th - 29th, 2026

So LA is well known for its food scene, and this spring break I had the opportunity to try out dishes from a variety of cuisines. Recently, i’ve become obsessed with the app Beli where you rank restaurants and get a map of restaurants you’ve visited.

Flamebachi

Located next to my hotel, this restaurant specializes in hibachi. I ordered a fried rice bowl with seared tuna and grilled veggies with garlic butter and lava sauce. The garlic butter made the texture of the tuna more indulgent and rich, and the lava sauce was told to be “extremely spicy” but I personally did not find it spicy. Maybe I just have a higher spice tolerance from Chinese food. Still enjoyed it, though. If i ever go to LA again, I’ll definitely be hitting Flamebachi up.

It’s Boba Time

About a 5-minute walk from my hotel, I decided to come here and grab some boba since I was craving some. I wasn’t in the mood for something too sugary or heavy, so I got the blue butterfly lemonade tea with popping boba. Always loved popping boba, especially the texture and how it bursts in my mouth.

CAVA

After a morning of museum hopping, I decided to head right over to USC village to grab some food. i’ve always wanted to try CAVA, since it seems pretty popular right now. I feel like it’s kinda like Sweetgreen, but more Mediterranean. I believe I got a harissa chicken bowl. It’s not jaw-droppingly good, but I would definitely eat there again.

Yobosoyo Superette

After grabbing CAVA, I decided to visit this nearby tea shop. I love how it has so many creative drink ideas, including yuzu cold brew. I was tempted to grab a yuzu cold brew, but I was cutting back on my caffiene. So I grabbed a yuzu matcha spritz instead. It came with lychee jelly and I added crystal boba. Very refreshing for a such hot day.

Corporation Food Hall Ramen Bar

I ordered black garlic ramen with tempura shrimp. I love the smoked flavor that black garlic gives, and the crunchiness and texture of tempura shrimp. And that jammy egg? Chef’s kiss. Only problem though was that it’s very filling, which made it harder to finish at the end. I was able to finish all the noodles and toppings, but not the soup.

Pho @ Vietnamese Restaurant in Chinatown

I ordered pho with all the toppings: meatball, tendon, tripe. I added in mint leaves, green peppers, bean sprouts, and lime juice - as well as chili oil. Never really been a fan of hoisin or sriracha, I think they’re too sweet. I feel like it tastes pretty authentic and sometimes you gotta stray off the beaten path, look at something beyond TikTok recommendations, to find the best food.

vitacane

Initially, I was hesitant to get something from here because I thought it would be overly sweet and I’m more of a savory person. But I’m all about trying new things. I got a raspberry limojito pressed sugarcane juice and it was packed with flavor. Not too sweet at all. I wish I added more toppings, though.

Inka Wasi

I visited Inka Wasi, a Peruvian restaurant not far from my hotel. I got a ceviche w/ squid, shrimp, and fish. I like seafood, especially seafood with ✨texture✨. It was a nice cold and savory dish for a hot day, and very authentic as well.

Din Tai Fung

Saw this place trending all over Insta and TikTok. So naturally, I had to go. Lowkey going here humbled me because it showed me how bad I am at using chopsticks. The food was good, but pretty filling. I think my favorite was the seaweed and bean curd salad.

Ice cream shop @ Santa Monica mall

This ice cream shop was called “the best ice cream in America”, so I wanted to try it and see if it was really true. Got matcha ice cream. I do feel like it was good, but I wouldn’t say it’s the best in America. I feel like Jeni’s is better.

Rosemary Grill

Finally, I visited this Mediterranean restaurant that’s about a 7-minute walk from my hotel. I ordered a salmon wrap with fries on the side and I thought the hummus was alright, but the garlic sauce SLAPPED. As a spice fiend, I loved trying out their variety of hot sauces. There’s a special place in my heart for Mediterranean food, especially with how creamy and flavorful it is.
title: Eating my way through LA

content:
August 14-15, 2025

Spend 2 days with me in Toronto and Niagara Falls!

August 14 - Toronto

I spent most of the morning exploring the city, and got noodles for lunch at Chinatown. After lunch, I went to the Royal Ontario Museum.

I was especially drawn to the interior design section, and had the opportunity to explore interior design throughout different time periods. I also saw ancient Egyptian tombs, Greek and Roman statues, East Asian porcelain and pottery, and more. I finished this museum in about 3-4 hours, and highly recommend it.

After that, I walked along the lakefront, which reminded me of Chicago.

I also saw the CN tower…

…and took WAY too many pictures of the skyline.

For dinner, I had roti. One of my favorite things about Toronto is the food scene, especially exploring different cuisines.

August 15 - Niagara Falls

After visiting Toronto, I visited Niagara Falls - which straddles the US/Canada border. I found it surreal how one side of the falls was in the US and the other in Canada, and got some pictures of its breathtaking beauty:

After visiting the falls, we ate at Hakkalicious, a restaurant known for Hakka cuisine. I really liked the aesthetic and ambience of this restaurant. I ordered pad thai, but I also tried hot garlic chicken and chili chicken. I just really like Asian food in general (I may be biased).
title: 2 Days in Canada

content:
Last summer, I studied abroad at the Pembroke Cambridge Summer Programme. Cambridge is a nice city with lots to do, and here are some of my favorite spots!

Food

Aromi

Aromi is an Italian restaurant that specializes in pizza, and you can get some gelato here as well!

Fitzbillies

Fitzbillies is a coffee shop that also sells pastries, and there are a couple of them located all over campus.

Giggling Squid

Located in the City Centre, Giggling Squid is a Thai restaurant that serves dishes such as noodles and spring rolls.

Pho

What’s better than a nice warm bowl of pho on a 60-degree English “summer” day?

Pizza Pilgrims

Portions here were a little big for one person, but still really good. Also - don’t knock pasta on pizza until you try it!

Yori

Portions here were a little big for one person, but still really good. Also - don’t knock pasta on pizza until you try it!

Tourist Attractions

Fitzwilliam Museum

Located close to my accommodation, I really enjoyed viewing sculptures, paintings, and ancient artifacts in this museum! On the first floor was mostly sculptures from ancient Greece and Rome and pottery from Western Europe to the Middle East to East Asia, as well as armor from medieval Europe. The second floor was mostly paintings - historical paintings. A lot of these paintings focused on social commentary of their era, many of which had to do with the role of women in society. A painting that stood out to me was of a woman reading in nature, which represented how women (at the time) were expected to be connected to nature, and men were more associated with human culture, politics, and society. It seems very interesting because, although (unfortunately) gender stereotyping still occurs over certain occupations, the stereotypes have changed over the years. As I walked through the gallery, I saw paintings from many different perspectives. Many art museums focus on European paintings, since a lot of famous painters are from European countries. However, I had the opportunity to see paintings from around the world, and it felt great to see my culture represented in these museums.

Cambridge Marketplace

Here, there are a lot of shops where you can get food, clothes, jewelry, books, and souvenirs! I highly recommend checking it out, since I got a pair of earrings and a necklace here that I really like, as well as some good Thai, Chinese, Greek, and Turkish street food.

Punting on the River Cam

This one costs money, unfortunately, but I was able to get a nice view of a lot of colleges at Cambridge, and learn about their histories on the punting tour.

The Corpus Clock

I often walk past this clock, and find it quite interesting that it’s shaped like a grasshopper. Apparently the grasshopper is “eating up” time, which is clever.

So yeah, that’s my list of recs in Cambridge. If you ever end up visiting, be sure to check some of these things out!
title: Cambridge Recs - Food, Museums, and More!

August 13, 2025

Spend a day with me on this picturesque, car-free island!

Got there early in the morning via ferry and caught this view.

As soon as I arrived, I walked around downtown. I noticed that the streets had an old-timey, European feel in their architecture. There were no cars, and people got around mostly on bikes and horse-drawn carriages.

I hiked up the hill, and fell in love with Mackinac’s natural beauty.

At the very top of the hill, I walked through the woods. I also saw the British Landing, and learned a lot about the history of the island (including its role in the War of 1812)

I also visited the Nature Center, and got a nice view of Arch Rock:

And of course, ate a lot of fudge! If you ever visit Mackinac, you HAVE to try the fudge!

Visiting this beautiful, historic island was truly one of the highlights of this road trip.
title: Day Trip to Mackinac

content:
March 24-31, 2025

Here’s a post about what I did over spring break in Boston!

Institute of Contemporary Art

Since my hotel was in Seaport and the ICA was within walking distance and only $15 for students, I decided to give this one a visit. I just love contemporary art, since it’s so abstract, groundbreaking, and has so much room for interpretation. Some exhibits that really stood out to me was the Shakers photo gallery, where Shakers are a religious community that emphasizes communal living, celibacy, shared property, gender and racial equality. Seeing their community in photos gives me a glimpse into a peaceful, nature-connected world so different from my own. Another exhibit that caught my eye was the Roman Empire exhibit, which showed photos of Rome (I’ve always wanted to go to Italy) and its historical architecture.

Me, featuring a nice view of the seaport:

Grub Street Bookstore

After visiting the ICA, I walked around the neighborhood and found a cafe/bookstore called Grub Street. They have every genre imaginable, even if I am more of a nonfiction girlie interested in spirituality, design/architecture, current events, and cooking/baking. Here are some books that I really wanted to pick up, but didn’t because I unfortunately couldn’t fit them into my suitcase.

Views of the city:

Boston Tea Party Ships & Museum

I also visited the Boston Tea Party Museum, an interactive historical adventure which unfortunately I couldn’t get pics of other than the exterior, but I learned a lot about the history of Boston.

Faneuil Food Hall

After spending 2 hours at the Boston Tea Party museum, I got a poke bowl at Faneuil Food Hall (not pictured), which has a lot of street food and shops selling tourist merch and art.

Fuller Craft Museum

I also had an opportunity to visit the Fuller Craft Museum, a museum just outside Boston that features crafts and other handmade items. If you ever visit the Boston area, I highly recommend this museum.

New England Nature Hike

And last but not least, here are some breathtaking views of rural New England. I was going to go to the Bird Art Museum, but it was closed, so I went hiking on the nearby trail instead.
title: Spring Break in Boston

content:
When studying abroad at Cambridge, I’ve had a couple of opportunities to visit London. Here are some things you MUST do there:

Big Ben (pictured above)

As one of the most iconic sights of London, the Big Ben is well worth a visit. You can also get a nice view of the river.

Tower of London

Learn all about this 1,000+ year old castle, the famous criminals that inhabited its prisons, and take a look at the Crown Jewels (which unfortunately I was not allowed to get a picture of)!

Watch a show on the West End

I went with some friends to watch Les Mis, and it was one of the best experiences of my life. Truly breathtaking.

Tate Modern

The exhibits here are so modern and ground-breaking, and it’s also free!

National Gallery

Went here twice, loved it both times. It’s also free, highly recommend.

British Museum

Also went here twice, and I still didn’t get through the whole museum because it’s HUGE. Wish I could go back.

Borough Market

So many good eats here, the other day a friend & I got green juice here!

Covent Garden

Lots of shops, restaurants, bars, and even a market place! I got to sample some teas at this tea shop, which was one of my favorite memories from the trip.

Walk across Tower Bridge

St. Paul’s Cathedral

Although I didn’t actually go in, I was still able to get a great view of the architecture from the outside.

Chinatown

Lots of good food here, and I was able to get in touch with my culture.

The Alchemist

The Alchemist is a magic/alchemy-themed bar in Covent Garden, known for its creative drink presentations and theatrical atmosphere. I went with a friend and really enjoyed the experience — the espresso martini came with a playful twist, and the French dip sandwich was a great pairing.

Walk around Soho

Although I didn’t buy anything, I still had a great time walking around.

So, yeah. Here are all my recs for things to do in London, I wish I was able to do more, such as go on the London Eye, visit Notting Hill, and tour the Shakespeare Globe, but time is limited. Thanks for reading!
title: Things to do in London

content:
Spent New Year’s Eve in NYC and had the opportunity to visit a lot of tourist attractions. Since NYC is huge, I’ll be focusing on Manhattan only in this post, which is where I was most of the time. So, without further ado, here are some things to do in Manhattan!

Times Square

Times Square is a major commercial hub in the middle of Manhattan, full of billboards and flashing lights. Here, you can grab some street food or watch a Broadway show.

Soho

As the fashion hub of NYC, Soho features European-style architecture and cute cafes.

Central Park

Here, you have the opportunity to enjoy quietness and nature within the hustle and bustle of the big city.

Wall Street

Located in the Financial District, Wall Street is home to the New York Stock Exchange and, if you happen to visit around the holidays, an annual tree lighting.

Statue of Liberty

Although I could not get a good picture, I went on a cruise that gave me a view of the Statue of Liberty herself.

9/11 Museum

Located in the World Trade Center, the 9/11 Memorial & Museum serves as a rememberance for one of the darkest times in our nation’s history.

The Met

The Met is home to art from around the world, from medieval European armor to Chinese pottery to ancient Egyptian tombs.

Empire State Building

Get a breathtaking view of the city from one of the tallest buildings in the world.

So yeah, these are some of the main attractions in Manhattan that I recommend, however there are some things that I would like to do but didn’t have time for, like visiting the Museum of Modern Art and Madame Tussauds. I really enjoyed my time here in NYC, and it seems like a great place to move once I graduate.
title: Things to do in NYC (Manhattan)

content:
August 9-11, 2024

Last weekend in Europe, spent it in Amsterdam (and Brussels!)

Friday, August 9th

After my last class that day, I took the Eurostar to Amsterdam. I finally arrived at 11:30ish pm, and checked into my Airbnb. However, I found out that my powerbank died (like DIED died), and there was no way to recharge it. My phone was on 12% battery, and I only had an “American” charger. I was freaking out at this point because I had my Eurostar tickets to London on my phone, not to mention my London to Cambridge train tickets. So if my phone actually died, there was no way for me to get back home. And so I slept, or at least attempted to. My Airbnb was in a very touristy area, with a lot of bars and pubs. Between the stress I was facing over my charger situation and people at pubs yelling over soccer at 3 am, it was hard for me to get any sleep.

Saturday, August 10th

I “woke up” at 8 (notice how “woke up” is in quotes, because I didn’t get any actual sleep), and planned on getting coffee, breakfast, and a European charger. I saw some locals that owned a cafe right next to my Airbnb, and asked them where I could get a European charger. The lady was so nice and said she could charge my phone for me, recommended a place where i could get a charger, and told me to get some more rest. And so I did. (By the way, on the very slim chance that you’re reading this, I cannot thank you enough!!!) I slept for a couple more hours, picked up my newly charged phone, thanked her, and got myself a new charger and power bank.

After that, I got breakfast, and went to the Rijksmuseum. I saw paintings from the Netherlands, and other European countries. I also saw a lot of pottery, porcelain, and historical artifacts such as ship models and historical clothing. I also admired the architecture inside the Rijksmusem, the stained glass windows, and the library within.

I also had the opportunity to walk around Amsterdam and take pictures in front of canals. While I’m pretty tall for an American girl, coming to Amsterdam was one of the rare instances where I felt short. Dutch people are known for being really tall, and it definitely isn’t uncommon to see women over 6 feet.

I saw another museum, the Moco Museum. This one was a bit more of a modern art museum, and there were many interactive exhibits, such as a mirror exhibit, and some video exhibits.

At this point, I was so tired that I went back to my Airbnb and took a nap. After I woke up at around dinner time, I got some noodles, walked around the streets of Amsterdam, did some cheese sampling, and went out with friends for the rest of the night.

Sunday, August 11th

I woke up, got coffee and breakfast, and checked out of my Airbnb. I wish I was able to go to the Van Gogh Museum, but tickets were sold out, but I did get to go to the Heineken Experience. I learned a lot about the history of Heineken, toured the brewery, got to try some Heineken beers, and after that, I got to go to the rooftop and get a nice view of the city.

After that, I was about to go to the train station, then went on one last walk around the city. When I finally got on the train, I took the train from Amsterdam to Brussels, then Brussels to London. Between these two trains, I had a few hours, so I walked around Brussels, admired its architecture, but didn’t have time to do any actual touristy stuff (though I wish I did!)

I got back to London at 10:30ish pm, then got to Cambridge at around 1. And I had at 8:45 am class the following morning, so that’s fun. But it was worth it, because I got to experience a whole new part of the world. Stay tuned for more travels!
title: Weekend in Amsterdam

content:
August 3-4, 2024

Spend a weekend with me in the city of love!

Saturday, August 3rd

I’ve been having trouble sleeping lately, so I woke up at 8:30ish, running on like 5 hours of sleep. I walked to Cambridge Station, which was about a 20 min walk, and napped on the train. After arriving in London, I got an iced Americano and boarded the Eurostar.

After arriving in Paris, I ran into some…issues. I didn’t speak French, and took the metro in the opposite direction from where my Airbnb was. While on the metro, I realized. So I got off, and went in the correct direction. I also had some trouble checking into the Airbnb at first, but got all that sorted out later. I realized that I had booked tickets to the Catacombs, which I didn’t want to be late to, so I took the metro and met my friend there.

We met at 5:30 pm. While going down the stairs into the Catacombs, I noticed how the stairs would go on forever. As I thought they were about to end, they were like, “you know what, SIKE!” and kept on going. But eventually I did make it down, and saw a cave full of tombs and bones. It felt a little bit trypophobic to me, but I learned a lot about Parisian history. After the Catacombs tour, I was feeling thirsty, since I hadn’t drank water for hours. And so I grabbed an “elixir” drink from the gift shop. It was a nice fizzy drink with edible glitter in it, making it look like a real-life potion. It felt good, being able to finally quench my thirst.

Later that evening, we went to Shakespeare and Co., a bookstore. I found some really interesting books that I wish I could have bought, but sadly my suitcase was getting too full. So I got a tote bag instead. After that, we had dinner at a French cafe, where I got a pasta and my friend got pulled beef. After dinner, we decided to see a couple more tourist attractions in Paris, such as the Notre Dame and the Eiffel Tower. The Notre Dame was pretty close, so we just walked there. It was still being built after the fire, which happened 5 years before this trip. This was when it started raining, but we decided that we HAD to see the Eiffel Tower, so we took the metro there. Unfortunately, we couldn’t get a good view of it, since most of it was blocked off for the Olympics. After seeing all those attractions, I checked into my Airbnb, called it a night, and went to bed.

Sunday, August 4th

I woke up at 8:30, checked out of my Airbnb, and put on the “I ❤️ Paris” tank that I got at a souvenir shop last night with a pair of denim shorts as I got breakfast at a French cafe near the Louvre. I got sunny side up eggs, bacon, a side salad, and an iced Americano. After breakfast, I stayed at the Louvre for about two hours, and took a ton of pictures, but I wish I could have stayed longer, since I didn’t go through all the exhibits. But that would take AT LEAST 2 days, and we’re short on time.

I saw a lot of greek and roman statues, renaissance-era art, ancient pottery, inscriptions, and tablets. It was a magical experience. Of course, i had to get a pic of the Mona Lisa. The ceilings really stood out to me, since they were all high, with exquisite carvings and paintings on them. A specific exhibit that I really liked was that room where everything was gold, and the ceiling was decorated with the months of the year, the signs of the zodiac (I’m a Libra!) all in Latin, of course.

After the louvre, we went to the Victor Hugo Museum. It was nice and historical, I didn’t understand much french, but I had a nice look around and learned a lot about Victor Hugo and his life.

We stayed in Paris until about 4pm, and that was when we took the Eurostar back to London, and the train back to Cambridge. So, yeah, that was a recap of my weekend in Paris.
title: Weekend in Paris
